\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Self-Description Startup Machine]
\lean{Turing.exists_selfStartupTM}
\label{Turing.exists_selfStartupTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode.toK, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode.toK_machine, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.exists_selfStartupTMK, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.tableBitsK, Turing.unaryFin}
\difficulty{5}
For every effective code system $c$ for one-work-tape binary machines, there are natural
numbers $K$, a finite state set $P$, a deterministic binary machine $R$ with $K+3$ work
tapes, and an exit state in $P$ such that the following holds. For each code $\alpha$,
there are natural numbers $T$ and $B$ so that, for every binary input $w$, after exactly
$T$ steps on $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$, $R$ is in the exit state, its input-head position
is $1$, all work-head positions are $0$, its output is empty, its second work tape
stores the decoded machine's transition table, and its third work tape stores the unary
encoding of that machine's initial state shifted by two cells, with every other
work-tape cell blank. The exit state is not reached at any earlier time, the output
remains empty through time $T$, and the total space used by time $T$ is at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-Simulation with Linear Space Overhead]
\lean{Turing.exists_selfUniversal}
\label{Turing.exists_selfUniversal}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode.toK, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode.toK_toFinTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.exists_selfUniversalK, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For every effective code system $c$ for one-work-tape binary machines, there is a
finite-state deterministic binary machine $U_0$ such that for every code $\alpha$ there
is a positive integer $C$ with the following property. For every binary input $w$,
output word $y$, and natural numbers $t,s$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts
on input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ at time $t$ with output $y$ and uses exactly $s$
work-tape cells by time $t$, then $U_0$ halts on input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ with
output $y$ at some time $t'$ and uses at most $C(s+1)$ work-tape cells by time $t'$.
\end{theorem}
